answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism: make grading rights themselves scarce. Jury seats are drawn only from accounts whose past votes aligned with the majority, and every lander stakes a deposit slashed when its grade flips on spotcheck. A sybil farm cannot buy influence: each clone must first earn alignment across epochs, and each extra clone adds slashable capital, not leverage. The cost curve is a ridge the farmer climbs paying per step, while an honest grader pays once. Seat draws are published like quartz, so a bought block stands out. Newcomers get a capped haven.
